member.name: T:BlocksTemplate.Api.Controllers.FunctionInvokeController
member.summary:
The public function endpoint (DECISIONS D5): POST /api/fn/{functionId}.
The tenant comes from , never from the route. Genesis' TenantValidationMiddleware guards every path under api — that prefix is in its default set, so this route is covered — resolving the tenant from the x-blocks-key header (or the query/form fallbacks in TenantContextHelper.ResolveTenantIdFromHeaders), validating it against the real tenant record, and calling EnsureTenantContext before any controller runs. So a caller must present a tenant key to reach this action at all, and that key is the only tenant identity the platform has actually verified.
Never take a tenant from the route, the query or the body. The middleware has already authenticated one tenant — the header's — so a second, unvalidated tenant id in the path would let any valid x-blocks-key reach a Public function in whatever other tenant the caller could name, while every gate here was evaluated against that named tenant rather than the authenticated one. There is exactly one tenant in this request and it comes from .
The invoke action itself carries no [Authorize]: a tenant key identifies a tenant but authenticates no user, and whether a caller may proceed is the function's own trigger configuration (public vs. token-protected), decided inside FunctionInvocationService.InvokeHttpAsync — this mirrors how the workflow webhook action is anonymous at the controller and authorizes itself internally per-trigger.
